leaves.why: The discriminant of $2x^2 + 3x + k = 0$ is $3^2 - 4(2)(k) = 9 - 8k$. The roots are real when it is $\geq 0$ and imaginary when it is $< 0$.
The discriminant of $kx^2 + 2x + 1 = 0$ is $2^2 - 4(k)(1) = 4 - 4k$. The roots are real when it is $\geq 0$ and imaginary when it is $< 0$. For $k = 0$ the equation is not quadratic.
The discriminant of $x^2 + 5x + k = 0$ is $5^2 - 4(1)(k) = 25 - 4k$. The roots are real when it is $\geq 0$ and imaginary when it is $< 0$.

Let $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} = k$, so $a = kb$ and $c = kd$. Then $\dfrac{2a + 3b}{2a - 3b} = \dfrac{2kb + 3b}{2kb - 3b} = \dfrac{2k + 3}{2k - 3}$ and in the same way $\dfrac{2c + 3d}{2c - 3d} = \dfrac{2k + 3}{2k - 3}$.

leaves.answer: Proved: both ratios equal $(pk + q) : (mk - n)$.
leaves.why: Let $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} = k$, so $a = kb$ and $c = kd$. Then $pa + qb : ma - nb = b(pk + q) : b(mk - n) = (pk + q) : (mk - n)$ and in the same way $pc + qd : mc - nd = d(pk + q) : d(mk - n) = (pk + q) : (mk - n)$.

leaves.answer: Proved: each ratio equals $\dfrac{b(f - d) + (cd - af)}{e(f - d)}$.
leaves.why: Let each ratio be $k$: $a - b = k(d - e)$ and $b - c = k(e - f)$. Then $a = b + k(d - e)$ and $c = b - k(e - f)$. So $b(f - d) + cd - af = bf - bd + bd - kd(e - f) - bf - kf(d - e) = -k(de - df + df - ef) = -ke(d - f) = ke(f - d)$. Dividing by $e(f - d)$ gives $k$.
Write $\dfrac{3 x - 2}{2 x^{2} - x} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{2 x - 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 2$, $B = -1$.
Write $\dfrac{x - 1}{x^{2} + 6 x + 5} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 5}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = - \dfrac{1}{2}$, $B = \dfrac{3}{2}$.
Write $\dfrac{1}{x^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $B = - \dfrac{1}{2}$.
Write $\dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 4 x - 5} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 5}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{1}{6}$, $B = \dfrac{5}{6}$.
Write $\dfrac{4 x + 2}{2 x^{2} + 3 x - 2} = \dfrac{A}{x + 2} + \dfrac{B}{2 x - 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{6}{5}$, $B = \dfrac{8}{5}$.

Write $\dfrac{x^{2} + 5 x + 3}{x^{3} + x^{2} - x - 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1} + \dfrac{C}{(x + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{9}{4}$, $B = - \dfrac{5}{4}$, $C = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Write $\dfrac{x^{2} + 2}{x^{3} + 7 x^{2} + 16 x + 12} = \dfrac{A}{x + 3} + \dfrac{B}{x + 2} + \dfrac{C}{(x + 2)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 11$, $B = -10$, $C = 6$.

Write $\dfrac{2 x - 1}{x^{3} - 6 x^{2} + 9 x} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{x - 3} + \dfrac{C}{(x - 3)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = - \dfrac{1}{9}$, $B = \dfrac{1}{9}$, $C = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

The fraction is improper, so divide first: quotient $1$, remainder $- 2 x - 1$. Write $\dfrac{- 2 x - 1}{x^{2} + 2 x + 1} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{(x + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = -2$, $B = 1$.

Write $\dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{3} - x^{2} - x + 1} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x - 1} + \dfrac{C}{(x - 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{1}{4}$, $B = \dfrac{3}{4}$, $C = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
Write $\dfrac{1}{x^{3} + x} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 1$, $B = -1$, $C = 0$.

Write $\dfrac{x^{2} + 3 x + 1}{x^{3} - x^{2} + 3 x - 3} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 3}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{5}{4}$, $B = - \dfrac{1}{4}$, $C = \dfrac{11}{4}$.

Write $\dfrac{2 x + 1}{x^{3} - x^{2} + x - 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{3}{2}$, $B = - \dfrac{3}{2}$, $C = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Write $- \dfrac{3}{x^{4} + 5 x^{2}} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{x^{2}} + \dfrac{C x + D}{x^{2} + 5}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 0$, $B = - \dfrac{3}{5}$, $C = 0$, $D = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Write $\dfrac{3 x - 2}{3 x^{3} + 12 x^{2} + x + 4} = \dfrac{A}{x + 4} + \dfrac{B x + C}{3 x^{2} + 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = - \dfrac{2}{7}$, $B = \dfrac{6}{7}$, $C = - \dfrac{3}{7}$.

Write $\dfrac{5 x}{x^{5} + x^{4} - 4 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 4 x + 4} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} - 2} + \dfrac{D x + E}{(x^{2} - 2)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = -5$, $B = 5$, $C = -5$, $D = -5$, $E = 10$.

Write $\dfrac{5 x^{2} - 4 x + 8}{x^{5} - 2 x^{4} + 2 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + x - 2} = \dfrac{A}{x - 2} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{D x + E}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{4}{5}$, $B = - \dfrac{4}{5}$, $C = - \dfrac{8}{5}$, $D = 1$, $E = -2$.

Write $\dfrac{4 x - 5}{x^{4} + 8 x^{2} + 16} = \dfrac{A x + B}{x^{2} + 4} + \dfrac{C x + D}{(x^{2} + 4)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 0$, $B = 0$, $C = 4$, $D = -5$.

Write $\dfrac{8 x^{2}}{- x^{6} - x^{4} + x^{2} + 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1} + \dfrac{C x + D}{x^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{E x + F}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = -1$, $B = 1$, $C = 0$, $D = 2$, $E = 0$, $F = -4$.

Write $\dfrac{2 x^{2} + 4}{x^{5} - x^{4} + 2 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} + x - 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{D x + E}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = \dfrac{3}{2}$, $B = - \dfrac{3}{2}$, $C = - \dfrac{3}{2}$, $D = -1$, $E = -1$.

The fraction is improper, so divide first: quotient $2$, remainder $2$. Write $\dfrac{2}{x^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 1$, $B = -1$.

The fraction is improper, so divide first: quotient $2 x + 3$, remainder $14 x + 2$. Write $\dfrac{14 x + 2}{x^{2} - 3 x + 2} = \dfrac{A}{x - 2} + \dfrac{B}{x - 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 30$, $B = -16$.
Write $\dfrac{3 x - 1}{x^{3} - 2 x^{2} + x} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{x - 1} + \dfrac{C}{(x - 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = -1$, $B = 1$, $C = 2$.
Write $\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} - 2 x + 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{(x - 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 1$, $B = 2$.
Write $\dfrac{2 x^{2}}{x^{4} - 4} = \dfrac{C x + D}{x^{2} + 2} + \dfrac{A x + B}{x^{2} - 2}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 0$, $B = 1$, $C = 0$, $D = 1$.

Write $\dfrac{3 x^{2} + 3 x + 2}{x^{4} - 1} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1} + \dfrac{C x + D}{x^{2} + 1}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 2$, $B = - \dfrac{1}{2}$, $C = - \dfrac{3}{2}$, $D = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Write $\dfrac{x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 1}{x^{4} + 2 x^{2} + 1} = \dfrac{A x + B}{x^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{C x + D}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 1$, $B = 3$, $C = -1$, $D = -2$.

The fraction is improper, so divide first: quotient $2$, remainder $- 2 x^{2} - 1$. Write $\dfrac{- 2 x^{2} - 1}{x^{3} + x^{2}} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x} + \dfrac{C}{x^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = -3$, $B = 1$, $C = -1$.
Write $\dfrac{4 x^{2} + 3 x + 14}{x^{3} - 8} = \dfrac{A}{x - 2} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 2 x + 4}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 3$, $B = 1$, $C = -1$.

Write $\dfrac{x^{4} + 3 x^{2} + x + 1}{x^{5} + x^{4} + 2 x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + x + 1} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B x + C}{x^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{D x + E}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}$. Multiply by the denominator and compare coefficients: $A = 1$, $B = 0$, $C = 0$, $D = 1$, $E = 0$.

$A \cup B = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$, so $(A \cup B)' = U - (A \cup B) = \{6, 7\}$, and $A' \cap B' = \{5, 6, 7\} \cap \{1, 2, 6, 7\} = \{6, 7\}$. leaves.answer: Class interval 5 (frequency distribution of the 30 weights): 21–25: 5; 26–30: 5; 31–35: 6; 36–40: 8; 41–45: 6.
leaves.why: The smallest weight is 22 and the largest is 43, so five classes of width 5 start at 21. Tally the 30 weights into the classes; the frequencies add up to 30.

leaves.answer: Histogram: draw touching rectangles on the class boundaries 20.5, 25.5, 30.5, 35.5, 40.5, 45.5 with heights 5, 5, 6, 8, 6. Frequency polygon: join the points (class mark, frequency) = (23, 5), (28, 5), (33, 6), (38, 8), (43, 6), and close the polygon at (18, 0) and (48, 0).
leaves.why: Class boundaries are half a unit below the lower limit and above the upper limit of each class. The frequency polygon is drawn through the mid-points of the tops of the rectangles and joined to the x-axis one class mark before the first class and after the last one.
Tally the 20 wages in classes of width 10 starting at 55, then add the frequencies down the column: the last cumulative frequency is 20.

leaves.answer: Plot the points (upper class boundary, cumulative frequency) = (64.5, 2), (74.5, 5), (84.5, 11), (94.5, 15), (104.5, 18), (114.5, 18), (124.5, 19), (134.5, 19), (144.5, 19), (154.5, 20), start the polygon at (54.5, 0) and join the points with straight lines.
leaves.why: A cumulative frequency (less than) polygon uses the upper class boundaries on the x-axis and the cumulative frequencies on the y-axis.
Write each class with its frequency and add the frequencies: $3 + 20 + 11 + 4 + 5 = 43$.
The gap between the classes is 1 (116 to 117), so half of it, 0.5, is subtracted from each lower limit and added to each upper limit.

leaves.answer: Median $= 121.125$ (≈ 121.13), Mode $= 119.77$, Harmonic mean ≈ 122.36, Geometric mean ≈ 122.48 (all in Rs).
leaves.why: Median: $n/2 = 21.5$ lies in the class 117–121 (boundaries 116.5–121.5, $f = 20$, cumulative frequency before it 3), so $\text{Median} = 116.5 + \dfrac{21.5 - 3}{20} \times 5 = 121.125$. Mode: the modal class is 117–121, so $\text{Mode} = 116.5 + \dfrac{20 - 3}{(20 - 3) + (20 - 11)} \times 5 = 119.77$. With the class marks $x$ = 114, 119, 124, 129, 134: $\text{H.M.} = \dfrac{n}{\sum f/x} = 122.36$ and $\text{G.M.} = \text{antilog}\left(\dfrac{\sum f \log x}{n}\right) = 122.48$.
E is the mid-point of $\overline{AC}$, so $AE = 4$ cm. In the right triangle $ABE$ (right angle at $A$): $BE^2 = AB^2 + AE^2 = 25 + 16 = 41$.
Apollonius theorem in $\Delta ABC$ with $BC^2 = 25 + 64 = 89$: $AB^2 + BC^2 = 2(BE^2 + AE^2)$, so $25 + 89 = 2(BE^2 + 16)$, $BE^2 = 57 - 16 = 41$.
